bug_semantics: is_url_safe normalized an attacker-controlled raw URL by deleting every @ before WHATWG URL parsing. For a URL such as http://evil.com@127.0.0.1/, this destroyed the userinfo/host delimiter and made validation inspect the fabricated hostname evil.com127.0.0.1, while a caller using the original URL connected to the internal host. The same pre-parse deletion also affected redirect validation.
flaw_origin: Commit 6885ccae01fbc1f2ca596faf50d541cddcfb671a first created src/helpers.ts and introduced both remove_at_symbol_in_string and its pre-parse use in is_url_safe and is_redirect_safe. Its immediate parent 9901fff9a4bca05fa99fc311f9e57971c33c17ff is present and has no src/helpers.ts, so this is the smallest surviving public first-write object. Later commit 3d4c9b93965267df1769eb0e9754c09ffc1e8055 rewrote the surrounding function but preserved the already-vulnerable operation and is not the BIC.

GitHub's exact BIC API record maps the author to HackingRepo, the committer to web-flow, verifies the signed payload, shows parent 9901fff9a4bca05fa99fc311f9e57971c33c17ff, and exposes no AI attribution; the exact commit-comments endpoint returns an empty list.

The npm 1.0.3 tarball's shipped dist/helpers.js contains u = remove_at_symbol_in_string(u), while the 1.0.4 tarball contains parsed.username/password rejection and omits that call from is_url_safe, independently closing the affected/fixed release boundary despite stale npm gitHead metadata.
